reviewer: OMP agent (M15 development and release images)
note: IMAGE-004 build root filesystem: src/images/rootfs.zig exports a locked runtime manifest as a tree and checks both directions of closure - every declared object present with the digest the manifest declared, and nothing undeclared in the tree, which is the direction that rots because a directory listing collects whatever was lying around. Paths are validated before anything is written: absolute paths, .., and empties are refused, because an export writes into a destination and a path that escapes it writes somewhere nobody asked for. The executable bit is applied from the manifest rather than inherited from the umask, and a manifest whose entry point is not marked executable is refused before the export exists. The entry point is then actually run from the exported tree, so the rootfs is a program's home rather than a directory of files. Evidence is recorded inside the WSL2 guest through scripts/wsl-evidence.ps1: actualPlatform and platformRole are both linux-x86_64, so the observation is of the platform the case names rather than of the host. Fault proof: dropping the executable requirement exports a rootfs whose entry point cannot run and the refusal assertion fails (exit 1); revert byte-identical against a backup, no FAULT markers remain.
